observations: body L1-L4: the end of Abraham bar Ḥiyyā's words begun on p. 302. «Albatenii» and «al–Battānī», divided between L3 and L4, are letter-spaced; «al–Battānī» has a long dash (5.2 pt). The r of «dirutae» (L3) prints broken.

body L5-L20: the dash after «III.» measures 10.3 pt; «Arabes», «Indis», «Ḥabash», «Muḥammad», «at–Tanūkhī», «Ibn al–Adamī» and «Ṣā‘id ibn al–Ḥasan» are letter-spaced; «Al–Battānī» (L5) and «al–Andalusī» (L18) are not. The long dashes of «Al–Battānī», «al–Qifṭī», «as–Sindhind» (L8, L13), «at–Tanūkhī», «al–Adamī» and «al–Ḥasan» measure 4.2 to 5.5 pt, that of «al–Andalusī» 4.1 pt. The i of «librum» (L18) did not print; a gap of its width stands in its place. By the tabular calendar counted from 15 July 622, the year 308 of the Hiǵrah began on 22 May 920, as printed (23 May from 16 July 622).

body L21-L30: «Thābit ibn Qurrah», «Alpetragius», «Hermetis», «Ricci», «Abraham Zachut» and «Hermes», divided between L28 and L29, are letter-spaced; «301–02» has a long dash (5.3 pt). The 7 beginning L30 prints with a broken foot.

notes_left L1-L8: «Āryabhaṭa», «Colebrooke», «Whitney» and «Martin» are letter-spaced; «244-48» has a hyphen (3.2 pt), and «482-» and «-90» (L6-L7) have hyphens (3.4 and 3.2 pt), as printed; «Sūrya-Siddhānta» has a hyphen of 3.4 pt.

notes_left L9-L18: «Suter» (L9, L15, L16), «Ibn al-Qifṭī», «Casiri», «Sédillot», «Oloug Beg» and «Ibn al–Qifṭī» (L18) are letter-spaced; «196-97», «Arabico-Hispana», «1760--70», «429-30», «103-07» and «Iul.-Aug.» have hyphens (3.0 to 4.1 pt), «al-Qifṭī» (L11) one of 3.0 pt and «al–Qifṭī» (L18) a long dash (4.4 pt). The full stop after «pag» (L14) prints only as a speck below the line. The month Shawwāl of 462 of the Hiǵrah ran from 13 July to 10 August 1070 (Julian, by the tabular calendar), as printed.
notes_right L1-L2: «Sédillot» is letter-spaced. «teuns» (L2) is printed so and kept; the word is a misprint.

notes_right L3-L10: «Delambre», «Isaacus Israelita» are letter-spaced; «73-75» and «Iudaeo-Hispanus» have hyphens (3.4 and 3.1 pt). The transliteration «Yiṣḥāq ben Yōsēph Yiçrĕ’ēlī» is set as printed, with ç and the macrons over ō, ē and ī. Isaac Israeli wrote the Yesod ha-‘olam at Toledo in 1310, as printed.
notes_right L11-L18: «Ricii», «Riccioli» and «Martin» are letter-spaced; the dash before «Ricci» measures 8.0 pt.
